recipes.title: Pool Party Margarita Slush
recipes.author: Kenneth and Claude
recipes.description: Frozen margarita engineered for the Ninja Slushi FS300 — a deliberately strong batch that still freezes, because the ratios respect the machine's chemistry window: real sugar builds the slush, too much booze breaks it. Three flavors, one physics: pick classic lime, mango, or strawberry below.

steps.title: Chill everything
steps.content: Mixers in the fridge, tequila in the freezer for 20 minutes. At 12.5% ABV this is mandatory, not a nice-to-have — a warm batch can take an hour to set; a cold one takes 30–45 minutes.

steps.title: Stir the batch
steps.content: Combine everything for your flavor in a pitcher and stir until the sweetener fully dissolves.

steps.title: Load the Slushi
steps.content: Pour into the vessel — stay under the 64 oz max fill line — and press Spiked Slush.

steps.title: Wait for texture, salt the rims
steps.content: 30–45 minutes to slush at this strength. Meanwhile: lime wedge around each cup rim, twist in the salt plate (or Tajín). Rim a stack before guests arrive.

steps.title: Rescue step (if needed)
steps.content: Still liquid at 45 minutes, or temp lights flashing / beeping about alcohol? Add ½ cup cold water — that drops the batch to ~12% and it will set. Then dispense and serve.

notes.title: The machine's chemistry window
notes.body: The Slushi freezes the mix partially and scrapes off ice crystals, which only works in a window: sugar at or above ~4–5 g/100 ml and alcohol between ~8% and ~14% on Spiked Slush. Under 8% it freezes brick-solid; over 14% it spins forever. All three flavor builds land at 12.2–12.6% ABV — deliberately strong, inside the window, on the slow side to set.

notes.title: No diet anything
notes.body: Sugar is structural, not just flavor — it's the antifreeze that keeps the batch scrapeable. Sugar-free limeade or diet mixers will trip the low-sugar alert or freeze into a block.

notes.title: Classic lime math
notes.body: 10 g/100 ml sugar, 12.5% ABV — the reference build the freeze window was tuned around.

notes.title: Why no agave here
notes.body: Mango nectar carries ~13 g/100 ml sugar on its own; adding syrup would push the batch too sweet. Lands at ~8.3 g/100 ml sugar, 12.6% ABV.

notes.title: Purée math
notes.body: Strawberry purée carries less sugar than nectar, so the ¼ cup agave comes back. Lands at ~8.2 g/100 ml sugar, 12.2% ABV. Sweetened purée: skip the agave.

notes.title: These are real drinks
notes.body: Each 8 oz cup carries about 2.5 oz of tequila-equivalent wearing a slushie costume. Say so at the party.

notes.title: Party ops
notes.body: Leave the machine running between pours — it holds texture for hours. Mix a SECOND flavor as a stirred pitcher in the fridge and top up the vessel as the level drops; all three builds match ABV, so refills keep the texture stable.

notes.title: Session-strength remix
notes.body: For an all-afternoon pace: drop the tequila to 1½ cups and add ¾ cup of the flavor base — lands near 9%, freezes faster, and shrugs off warm refills.

recipes.title: Loco Moco
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Hawaiian diner classic — seared patty and a fried egg over rice, drowned in brown gravy. This build makes the gravy gluten-free (cornstarch, no roux) and leans it out with 90/10 beef and mushrooms doing the richness work instead of butter.

ingredients.name: GF Worcestershire sauce, mixed into the meat
cornstarch, whisked with 3 tbsp cold water into a slurry
large eggs, fried over-easy (1 per person)

steps.title: Season and form patties
steps.content: Mix seasoning + Worcestershire into the beef, form 3 patties (don't overwork — keeps them tender since lean beef has less fat to carry toughness).

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Hot skillet, no oil needed (beef renders enough). Sear ~3–4 min per side to medium — lean beef overcooks fast, don't walk away. Rest on a plate.

steps.title: Build the gravy base
steps.content: Same skillet, add butter, then onion and mushrooms. Cook 5–6 min until mushrooms are browned and onion is soft, scraping up the fond.

steps.title: Garlic
steps.content: Add garlic, 30 seconds until fragrant.

steps.title: Deglaze
steps.content: Pour in broth + Worcestershire, scrape the pan clean, bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Thicken
steps.content: Re-whisk the cornstarch slurry (it settles) and stir in. Simmer 1–2 min until glossy and coats the back of a spoon. Taste, adjust salt/pepper.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.content: Fry over-easy in a separate pan while the gravy finishes.

steps.title: Build bowls
steps.content: Rice or cauliflower rice → patty → gravy ladled over → fried egg on top → green onion.

notes.title: GF check
notes.body: Most major Worcestershire brands (Lea & Perrins US bottle) are labeled gluten-free, but always check the label — malt vinegar shows up in some formulations. Coconut aminos + a dash of fish sauce is a solid substitute.

notes.title: Why mushrooms
notes.body: Classic loco moco gravy leans on pan drippings + butter for richness. Mushrooms add body and umami for very little fat — the main "healthier" lever here besides the leaner beef.

notes.title: Kristen build
notes.body: Swap white rice for steamed cauliflower rice. Same patty, egg, and gravy — already lean. For an even lighter bowl, skip the rice base entirely and add extra mushrooms.

notes.title: Egg doneness
notes.body: Over-easy is classic (yolk breaks into the gravy). Hard-fried works fine for meal-prep/reheating.

notes.title: Make-ahead
notes.body: Double the gravy batch and freeze half — it reheats cleanly and is the slowest part to make from scratch on a weeknight.

recipes.title: Coffee Crème Brûlée
recipes.author: Ken, Madison and Claude
recipes.description: v2 with one ingredient swap: half the instant espresso becomes unsweetened cocoa. The chocolate doesn't dominate — it deepens the coffee, lands somewhere between coffee and mocha. Tested 2026-05-09; confirmed keeper.

steps.title: Preheat the bath
steps.content: Preheat sous vide bath to 176°F (80°C). Set out six 4 oz wide-mouth mason jars with lids and rings.

steps.title: Heat cream and dissolve
steps.content: In a saucepan over medium-low, warm the cream until steaming (do not boil). Off heat, whisk in the instant espresso AND cocoa powder until fully dissolved and no lumps remain. The cocoa needs the heat to bloom properly.

steps.title: Whisk the yolks
steps.content: In a medium bowl, whisk the yolks, sugar, and salt until pale and ribbony.

steps.title: Temper
steps.content: Whisking constantly, stream the hot mocha cream into the yolks slowly — first tablespoon at a time, then build up.

steps.title: Finish the base
steps.content: Whisk in the vanilla. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a pourable vessel — this catches any cocoa lumps. Skim any foam.

steps.title: Fill the jars
steps.content: Divide custard among the 6 jars, leaving ½ inch of headspace. Cap with lids and rings — finger-tight only.

steps.title: Sous vide
steps.content: Lower jars into the 176°F bath. Cook for 1 hour.

steps.title: Ice bath and chill
steps.content: Transfer to an ice bath for 15 minutes. Refrigerate at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

steps.title: Brûlée and serve
steps.content: Sprinkle 1 tbsp of turbinado sugar evenly across each. Torch in tight circles until deep amber. Rest 1 minute.

notes.title: Why cocoa
notes.body: The cocoa adds dark-chocolate depth without making this a chocolate dessert. With 1 tbsp cocoa + 1 tbsp espresso, coffee and chocolate share the spotlight. Going 2 tbsp cocoa + 0 espresso would push it fully into chocolate-pudding territory; 0 cocoa + 2 tbsp espresso is v2.

notes.title: Cocoa choice
notes.body: Use unsweetened. Dutched works well — its smoother, less acidic profile pairs nicely with the espresso. Avoid drinking cocoa, which has sugar and milk solids that throw off the custard set.

notes.title: Strain matters here
notes.body: Cocoa wants to clump. Strain through a fine mesh after dissolving and again after tempering if you see specks. Smooth custard = clean spoon-coat.

notes.title: Why 176°F / 80°C
notes.body: Sweet spot for crème brûlée texture — yolks set without scrambling, no skin, no grain.

notes.title: Espresso dosing
notes.body: Same brand recommendations as v2 — Mount Hagen, Starbucks VIA Italian Roast, Nescafé Gold, Waka. Espresso roast deepens the chocolate notes; standard instant coffee works too but flatter.

notes.title: Make-ahead
notes.body: Custards hold 3 days in the fridge before brûlée. Don't torch until serving.

recipes.title: Mexican Meat Slop
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: A workhorse — tacos, burritos, nachos, or over rice. Sun-dried tomatoes and chipotles do the heavy lifting.

ingredients.name: chipotle peppers in adobo (chopped, with sauce)

steps.title: Sweat the onion
steps.content: Cook diced onion in a pan over medium heat until softened and translucent, ~3 min.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Add ground beef, break up with a spoon, brown fully.

steps.title: Add spices
steps.content: Add cumin, paprika, garlic powder, taco seasoning, salt, and pepper. Stir to combine.

steps.title: Add aromatics
steps.content: Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and chipotles with adobo sauce. Cook 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.content: Pour in beef stock, simmer 5–7 minutes until liquid is mostly absorbed. Taste and adjust seasoning.

notes.title: Serving
notes.body: Great for tacos, burritos, nachos, or over rice.

notes.title: Heat dial
notes.body: Two chipotles = noticeable warmth. Bump to three if you want sweat.

recipes.title: Protein Mashed Potatoes
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Yukon Golds with cottage cheese and Fairlife doing the protein work. Ricer, not mixer — gluey potatoes are a tragedy.

ingredients.name: sour cream or lite cream cheese

steps.title: Boil
steps.content: Boil potatoes and whole garlic cloves in well-salted water until fork-tender, ~15–20 min.

steps.title: Drain and dry
steps.content: Drain. Return to hot pot for a minute to evaporate residual water.

steps.title: Blend dairy
steps.content: Blend cottage cheese, Fairlife, sour cream (or lite cream cheese), and butter until completely smooth — no curds.

steps.title: Rice
steps.content: Pass potatoes and softened garlic through a ricer back into the pot.

steps.title: Fold and season
steps.content: Fold in the smooth dairy mixture. Season with salt, white pepper, and onion salt to taste.

notes.title: Texture rule
notes.body: Ricer only. Hand mixer breaks the starch and turns this into glue.

notes.title: Critical step
notes.body: Dairy mixture must be blended completely smooth before folding in. No shortcuts.

notes.title: White pepper
notes.body: Keeps the color clean and adds a subtle, earthy heat that pairs well with the creaminess.

recipes.title: Carne Asada
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Thin-sliced cross rib with citrus, cilantro, and a non-traditional splash of soy for umami. Cast iron, screaming hot.

steps.title: Make marinade
steps.content: Whisk all marinade ingredients together. Add meat, coat well.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.content: Refrigerate 2–3 hours. Max 4 — citrus starts breaking down texture beyond that.

steps.title: Temper
steps.content: Pull from fridge, pat dry, rest at room temp 15 minutes.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Cast iron screaming hot. 2 minutes per side for deep char.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.content: Rest 5 minutes. Slice against the grain. Finish with fresh lime and reserved cilantro.

notes.title: Soy sauce
notes.body: Adds umami depth without making it taste Asian. Trust the process.

notes.title: Heat matters
notes.body: If the pan isn't smoking, the meat steams instead of searing. Wait for it.

recipes.title: Ken's Egg Salad
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Diced precise (¼"), Dijon-forward, with homemade pickled celery and onions doing the work. Self-referential — pulls from your pickled celery recipe.

steps.title: Boil and dice
steps.content: Hard boil eggs, peel, and dice into ¼-inch pieces.

steps.title: Make the dressing
steps.content: In a medium bowl, combine mayonnaise and Dijon mustard. Mix until smooth.

steps.title: Fold in eggs
steps.content: Add diced eggs to the dressing and fold gently to coat.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Season with salt, pepper, celery salt, garlic salt, onion salt, and paprika. Stir to combine.

steps.title: Add mix-ins
steps.content: Fold in diced hot pickles, pickled celery, and pickled onions.

steps.title: Rest
steps.content: Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour to allow flavors to combine before serving.

notes.title: Milder version
notes.body: Substitute regular dill pickles for Grillo's Hot.

notes.title: Self-referential
notes.body: This consumes your homemade pickled celery and onions — the pantry ecosystem at work.

recipes.title: Asian-Inspired Ground Beef Stir-Fry
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: A quick, savory weeknight stir-fry with Yoshida's marinade and Momofuku Chili Crunch, served over rice.

ingredients.name: Momofuku Chili Crunch chili oil, to taste
salt, pepper, garlic salt, to taste

steps.title: Sear the beef
steps.content: Sear the ground beef in a hot pan until golden brown. Season with salt, pepper, and garlic salt.

steps.title: Add shallots
steps.content: Add the sliced shallots and stir to combine.

steps.title: Add carrots
steps.content: Add the carrots and stir.

steps.title: Add cabbage
steps.content: Add the cabbage mix last and stir. Let everything cook down until the vegetables are tender.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.content: Pour in the Mr. Yoshida's sauce and let it come to a boil, allowing some liquid to cook off.

steps.title: Vinegar
steps.content: Add the rice vinegar and stir. Let the sauce thicken slightly.

steps.title: Finish with chili crunch
steps.content: Finish with Momofuku Chili Crunch to taste.

steps.title: Plate
steps.content: Serve over rice and top with sesame seeds.

notes.title: Vegetable swaps
notes.body: Any quick-cooking vegetables can be substituted for the carrots and cabbage.

notes.title: Heat dial
notes.body: Adjust the chili crunch to your preferred heat level.

recipes.title: Bacon Egg & Cheese Rice Paper Spiral
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: A crispy, gooey, melty breakfast treat inspired by NYC bodega bacon egg and cheese sandwiches.

steps.title: Scramble
steps.content: Scramble 4 eggs until just set, soft and fluffy — not dry. Set aside.

steps.title: Prep rice paper
steps.content: Whisk the remaining egg on a plate — this is your egg dip. One at a time, dip each rice paper sheet into the beaten egg, coating evenly. Lay them out on a lightly oiled cutting board, slightly overlapping to create one large sheet.

steps.title: Layer fillings
steps.content: Layer the scrambled eggs down the center, followed by chopped bacon and shredded mozzarella.

steps.title: Roll & shape
steps.content: Roll up tightly into a cylinder, sealing the edge as you go. Then gently curl it around itself into a compact spiral.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Brush the top with any leftover egg and sprinkle generously with everything bagel seasoning.

steps.title: Bake
steps.content: Bake at 400°F for 15–20 minutes until golden and crisp.

notes.title: Tip
notes.body: Work quickly with the egg-dipped rice paper before it gets too sticky.

notes.title: Bacon prep
notes.body: Make sure your bacon is fully cooked and chopped before starting.

recipes.title: Bread & Butter Pickles
recipes.author: Chef John (Food Wishes)
recipes.description: Chef John's classic refrigerator pickle — sweet, tangy, with a slow turmeric warmth. Makes about 2 pints.

ingredients.name: pickling cucumbers (or other firm, small cucumbers)

steps.title: Slice and salt
steps.content: Slice cucumbers into ¼-inch thick rounds. Combine in a large bowl with the sliced onion and jalapeños. Toss with the kosher salt, cover, and let sit at room temperature for 2 hours. This draws out excess moisture for crunchier pickles.

steps.title: Drain
steps.content: After 2 hours, drain the cucumbers well in a colander. Do not rinse. Pat dry with paper towels if desired.

steps.title: Make the brine
steps.content: In a saucepan, combine the vinegar, sugar, water, mustard seeds, celery seeds, peppercorns, turmeric, cloves, and garlic. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring to dissolve the sugar.

steps.title: Combine
steps.content: Add the drained cucumber mixture to the hot brine. Stir to combine and bring just back to a simmer.

steps.title: Jar
steps.content: Transfer the pickles and brine to clean mason jars, making sure the cucumbers are fully submerged in liquid. Let cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Refrigerate
steps.content: Cover and refrigerate. The pickles are ready to eat after 24 hours but improve with a few days of resting. Best flavor develops after 1 week.

notes.title: Storage
notes.body: Keeps refrigerated for several months.

notes.title: Sugar
notes.body: Can reduce to 1–1.5 cups for less sweet pickles.

notes.title: Heat
notes.body: Jalapeños are optional; omit for milder pickles.

notes.title: Canning
notes.body: For shelf-stable pickles, process in a water bath for 10 minutes. Refrigerator pickles need only soap-and-water cleaning of jars.

recipes.title: Caramelized Onion Pasta
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Jammy onions, chili crisp, cream, and a heavy parmesan finish. The original cream version — silky and rich.

steps.title: Mise en place
steps.content: Slice your onion, mince the garlic (use fresh), and measure out all your seasonings. Bring the cream or coconut milk to room temperature.

steps.title: Caramelize
steps.content: Heat 2 tbsp butter + 1 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the onions and let them cook for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until golden and jammy. If they stick, hit them with a splash of water.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.content: While onions caramelize, boil a pot of salted water and cook pasta until al dente. Drain, but reserve some pasta water — liquid gold.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.content: When onions are deeply golden, stir in the garlic and seasonings. Bloom for a minute, add chili crisp and sauté another minute. Pour in cream (or coconut milk). Simmer for a few minutes, then add the parmesan.

steps.title: Toss
steps.content: Add pasta to the sauce and toss to coat. Use reserved pasta water to loosen if too thick — silky, not sticky.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Serve hot with an extra spoon of chili crisp on top and parsley if you're feeling fancy.

notes.title: Onion patience
notes.body: 15–20 minutes of caramelization is the floor, not the ceiling. Deep golden = deep flavor.

recipes.title: Caramelized Onion Pasta
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Same jammy onions and chili crisp, but with blended cottage cheese standing in for cream. ~25g extra protein, no one will know.

steps.title: Mise en place
steps.content: Slice onion, mince garlic, measure seasonings. Blend cottage cheese and skim milk until completely smooth — this is your creamy base.

steps.title: Caramelize
steps.content: Heat butter + olive oil over medium. Add onions and cook 15–20 minutes until golden and jammy. Splash with water if they stick.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.content: Boil pasta to al dente in salted water. Reserve some pasta water before draining.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.content: Stir garlic and seasonings into golden onions, bloom for a minute. Add chili crisp, sauté one more minute. REMOVE FROM HEAT, let cool 1–2 minutes (this prevents curdling), then pour in the blended cottage cheese mixture. Stir, return to LOW heat, warm through gently — do not boil. Add parmesan.

steps.title: Toss
steps.content: Add pasta and toss. Loosen with reserved pasta water as needed.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Top with extra chili crisp and parsley.

notes.title: Protein boost
notes.body: The cottage cheese swap adds roughly 25g of protein to the entire dish compared to the cream version.

notes.title: Key tip
notes.body: Blend cottage cheese until silky smooth — no one will know it's there. Let the pan cool slightly before adding it to prevent curdling.

recipes.title: Chicken Gnocchi Soup
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Creamy, cozy, one-pot. Chicken seared in sun-dried tomato oil, finished with cream, gnocchi, spinach, basil, and a parmesan rind.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken
steps.content: Toss the chicken with sun-dried tomato oil and all the chicken seasonings. Let it marinate for as long as your patience can handle — or go straight to the pot.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Heat 4 tbsp olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken and cook until nicely browned on both sides. It should not yet be cooked through. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Sweat the vegetables
steps.content: In the same pot, add onion, celery, carrots, sun-dried tomatoes, garlic, and all veggie seasonings. Cook over medium for 8–10 minutes, stirring, until everything is soft. Stir in tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.

steps.title: Simmer the broth
steps.content: Pour in chicken broth and bring to a gentle simmer for 15 minutes. While it simmers, chop or shred the chicken. Add the chicken back, then slowly stir in the cream. Simmer another 5 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.content: Add gnocchi, parmesan, parmesan rind (if using), spinach, basil, and thyme. Squeeze in lemon juice. Simmer 5–10 minutes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Ladle into bowls and finish with black pepper, chili flakes, extra parmesan, and more basil. Serve with warm buttered bread.

notes.title: Cream temperature
notes.body: Bring cream to room temp before adding to prevent the soup from breaking when it hits the hot broth.

recipes.title: Chicken Protein Cheese Dip
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Cottage-cheese-blended cheese dip with chunk chicken, Hatch chilies, and adobo. Tailgate-friendly, weirdly high protein.

steps.title: Blend the base
steps.content: Add cottage cheese, Trader Joe's Three Cheese Blend, taco seasoning, water, and jalapeños with juice to a blender. Blend until smooth.

steps.title: Transfer
steps.content: Transfer blended cheese mixture to a sauce pot over medium heat.

steps.title: Add proteins
steps.content: Add the can of chunk chicken and the can of Hatch green chilies to the pot.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Season with adobo peppers, salt, garlic, garlic powder, onion powder, and a small amount of cayenne to taste.

steps.title: Heat through
steps.content: Stir to combine and heat through until warmed and well incorporated. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Coconut Macaroons
recipes.author: Once Upon a Chef
recipes.description: Soft and chewy on the inside, crisp and golden on the outside. Optional chocolate-dipped finish.

ingredients.name: sweetened flaked coconut (Baker's Angel Flake recommended)
sweetened condensed milk (¾ cup plus 2 tbsp)

steps.title: Preheat
steps.content: Preheat the oven to 325°F (165°C). Set two oven racks near the center. Line two baking sheets with parchment paper.

steps.title: Mix coconut base
steps.content: In a medium bowl, mix together the coconut, sweetened condensed milk, and vanilla extract. Set aside.

steps.title: Whip whites
steps.content: In the bowl of an electric mixer, beat the egg whites and salt until stiff peaks form.

steps.title: Fold
steps.content: Use a large rubber spatula to fold the egg whites into the coconut mixture until combined.

steps.title: Scoop
steps.content: Using a mini ice cream scoop or two spoons, form heaping tablespoons of the mixture into mounds on the prepared baking sheets, spacing about 1 inch apart.

steps.title: Bake
steps.content: Bake for 23–25 minutes, rotating the pans from top to bottom and front to back halfway through, until tops and edges are golden.

steps.title: Cool
steps.content: Let cool on the pans for a few minutes, then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.

steps.title: Optional: chocolate dip
steps.content: Melt chocolate in a microwave-safe bowl at medium power, 30-second intervals, until smooth. Dip the bottoms of cooled macaroons, return to the lined sheets, refrigerate 10 minutes to set.

notes.title: Parchment, not wax
notes.body: Macaroons stick to wax paper. Use parchment.

notes.title: Coconut brand
notes.body: Baker's Angel Flake is recommended — there's variability between brands.

notes.title: Storage
notes.body: Keeps in an airtight container at room temp for about a week.

notes.title: Freezing
notes.body: Freeze undipped for up to 3 months. Thaw before dipping in chocolate.

recipes.title: GF Air Fryer Fried Chicken
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Double-dredge cornstarch + crushed cornflakes for maximum crunch and adhesion. Fully gluten-free, finished with a sweet-savory honey garlic ginger dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: boneless skinless chicken thighs or breast
cornstarch (divided: ½ cup for dredge, ¼ cup for cornflake mix)
salt (½ tsp for chicken, ½ tsp for dredge)

steps.title: Prep the chicken
steps.content: Cut chicken into strips or chunks. For whole thighs or breasts, pound to 1-inch thickness or butterfly. Pat completely dry. Season directly with half the salt and pepper. Let rest 10–15 min at room temp.

steps.title: Set up breading stations
steps.content: Crush cornflakes to medium (panko-sized) consistency. Dish 1: ½ cup cornstarch + remaining salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, cayenne. Dish 2: beaten eggs. Dish 3: crushed cornflakes + remaining ¼ cup cornstarch.

steps.title: Double dredge
steps.content: Cornstarch (Dish 1, shake off excess) → egg (Dish 2, drip off) → cornflake mix (Dish 3, press firmly all sides). Place coated pieces on a wire rack while preparing the rest.

steps.title: Air fry — first side
steps.content: Preheat air fryer to 385°F for 3–5 min. Arrange chicken in a single layer with space between pieces. Spray tops generously. Cook 8 minutes.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.content: Flip carefully, spray again, cook 8 more minutes (16 total for 1-inch pieces). Verify internal temp reaches 165°F.

steps.title: Rest
steps.content: Transfer to a wire rack over a sheet pan. Rest 4–6 minutes — lets steam escape, prevents sogginess.

steps.title: Sauce
steps.content: Combine honey, soy sauce, rice vinegar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, and red pepper flakes in a small saucepan. Heat over medium-low about 3 minutes, stirring, until combined. Keep warm.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Serve chicken with sauce on the side for dipping. Coating it directly will soften the crust.

notes.title: Why double dredge
notes.body: The cornstarch in the final coating gives the cornflakes something to grip. Single dredge works but adhesion is better.

notes.title: Cornflake consistency
notes.body: Aim for panko-sized pieces. Too fine loses texture; too coarse won't adhere.

notes.title: Oil spray is essential
notes.body: Without it, cornflakes stay pale and chewy rather than golden and crisp.

notes.title: Verify GF
notes.body: Check that your cornflakes and soy sauce are certified gluten-free.

notes.title: Bone-in adjustment
notes.body: For bone-in pieces, increase cook time to 22–28 minutes total, flipping halfway.

recipes.title: GF French Beef Stew
recipes.author: Kenneth (adapted from @summer_food)
recipes.description: Classic French beef stew with mushrooms — adapted GF using tapioca starch in place of flour. Long simmer, glossy finish.

steps.title: Crisp the bacon
steps.content: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium. Add bacon and cook until crisp. Remove and set aside.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Season the beef chunks with salt and pepper. In the same pot, brown in batches to ensure each piece is well-seared. Remove and set aside with the bacon.

steps.title: Sweat aromatics
steps.content: In the same pot, add chopped onion, sliced carrots, and minced garlic. Cook until onion becomes translucent.

steps.title: Thicken with starch
steps.content: Sprinkle the tapioca starch over the vegetables and stir well, ensuring even coating and scraping the fond off the bottom of the pot.

steps.title: Combine and simmer
steps.content: Return beef and bacon to the pot. Stir in tomato paste, add bouquet garni. Pour in beef broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer, cover, and cook gently for about 2 hours.

steps.title: Mushrooms
steps.content: About 30 minutes before the stew is done, sauté mushrooms in oil in a separate pan until golden. Add to the stew and continue to simmer.

notes.title: Flour swap
notes.body: Tapioca starch is a clean 1:1 substitute — thickens without going gummy and leaves the broth glossy. Arrowroot or potato starch break down over long simmers; if using those, stir in as a slurry during the last 30 minutes.

notes.title: Bacon
notes.body: Look for a GF-certified label or check the ingredient list — flavorings/smoke additives can introduce gluten.

notes.title: Beef broth
notes.body: Store-bought broths sometimes contain hydrolyzed wheat protein. Use GF-certified or homemade.

recipes.title: Homemade Gyros Salad
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Air-fryer gyro meat (food-processor smooth) over romaine with tzatziki, feta, and a red wine vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: English cucumber (grated and squeezed very dry)

steps.title: Process the meat
steps.content: Blend all meat ingredients in a food processor until it becomes a smooth, sticky paste — this is what gives you the dense, sliceable texture.

steps.title: Air-fry
steps.content: Spread thin (~¼ inch) on parchment in your air fryer. Cook at 375°F for 12–15 minutes, flipping halfway. Browned and slightly crispy at the edges.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.content: Let rest a few minutes, then slice into strips.

steps.title: Tzatziki
steps.content: Combine all tzatziki ingredients. Letting it sit for 30 minutes improves the flavor significantly.

steps.title: Build the salad
steps.content: Build on a bed of chopped romaine with tomatoes, red onion, cucumber, olives, pepperoncini, feta, and parsley.

steps.title: Dress and top
steps.content: Drizzle with a simple red wine vinaigrette (3:1 olive oil to red wine vinegar, pinch of oregano, salt, pepper). Top with warm gyro meat strips and a generous dollop of tzatziki. Warm pita on the side if you want.

notes.title: Texture key
notes.body: The food processor paste is what gives sliceable, dense gyro meat. Don't skip the processing step.

recipes.title: Ken's Meat Sauce
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: A slow-simmered Sunday sauce — thyme, marjoram, rosemary, capers with their brine, lemon, and red wine vinegar bring layered acid and lift.

steps.title: Sweat the onion
steps.content: Heat olive oil in a Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium / medium-low. Add onions with a pinch of salt and cook ~5 minutes until translucent.

steps.title: Garlic
steps.content: Add garlic and cook for 1–2 minutes until fragrant.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Increase heat to medium. Add ground beef and cook, breaking it up, until no pink remains.

steps.title: Toast herbs
steps.content: Create a well in the center of the meat. Add thyme, marjoram, and rosemary to the well and toast until fragrant, ~30 seconds, then stir into the meat.

steps.title: Tomato paste
steps.content: Add tomato paste to the well and cook for 1 minute, stirring to incorporate.

steps.title: Crushed tomato + acids
steps.content: Add crushed tomatoes and stir. Add red wine vinegar, capers with juice, lemon juice. Stir well.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.content: Add bay leaves, bring to a low boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 3–4 hours, stirring occasionally. Add chicken stock as needed to maintain consistency.

steps.title: Finish
steps.content: Remove bay leaves (and herb sprigs if using fresh) before serving. Adjust salt to taste.

notes.title: The simmer is non-negotiable
notes.body: The long simmer is essential — it allows the acids to mellow, flavors to marry, and the sauce to develop body. Don't rush it.

recipes.title: Rosemary Breakfast Potatoes
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Crispy, herb-loaded breakfast potatoes — boiled first for a fluffy interior, then roasted at high convection heat for maximum crunch.

steps.title: Cut
steps.content: Halve each potato lengthwise, then halve each half lengthwise again (into quarters). Cut crosswise into ¼–⅓-inch thick slices.

steps.title: Boil
steps.content: Place potatoes in a large pot, cover with cold water, salt generously. Bring to a boil and cook until soft and tender throughout but not falling apart, ~10–12 minutes.

steps.title: Drain and season
steps.content: Drain well and return to the pot or a large bowl. Drizzle with olive oil and toss gently. Add salt, pepper, rosemary, garlic powder, and onion salt. Toss until evenly seasoned.

steps.title: Roast — first side
steps.content: Spread in a single layer on a sheet pan. Roast at 460°F convection for 15 minutes until bottoms are golden and crispy.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.content: Flip and roast 15 more minutes until deeply golden and crisp on both sides.

notes.title: Why boil-then-roast
notes.body: Boiling gelatinizes the starch so you get a creamy interior; the high convection heat crisps the edges fast.

notes.title: Slice thinness
notes.body: Keep slices thin (¼–⅓ inch) so they get plenty of surface area for browning.

notes.title: No convection?
notes.body: Bump the temp to 475°F and you may need a couple extra minutes per side.

recipes.title: Steak Bites with Cottage Cheese Alfredo
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Cast-iron seared steak cubes over fettuccine with a blender-only cottage-cheese alfredo. Higher protein, lower fat than a butter/cream/parm classic.

ingredients.name: light cream cheese (or ~6 wedges Laughing Cow Light)
garlic powder (preferred — or 2–3 fresh garlic cloves)

steps.title: Season the steak
steps.content: Pat steak cubes dry. Toss with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, and parsley until evenly coated. Let sit at room temp while you prep the sauce.

steps.title: Blend the alfredo
steps.content: Add cottage cheese, cream cheese, garlic powder, salt, pepper, and parsley to a high-speed blender. Blend on high for 3–5 minutes until completely smooth and warmed through — friction heats the sauce as it emulsifies.

steps.title: Heat the cast iron
steps.content: Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat (or preheat grill to high) until smoking. No oil needed if cast iron is well-seasoned; otherwise a teaspoon of high-smoke-point oil.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Sear steak cubes in a single layer, ~60–90 seconds per side for medium-rare. Work in batches if needed — do not crowd the pan or they'll steam. Transfer to a plate and let rest 2–3 minutes.

steps.title: Cook pasta
steps.content: Start cooking the pasta to al dente while the steak rests. Reserve ½ cup pasta water before draining.

steps.title: Toss
steps.content: Toss drained pasta with alfredo sauce, thinning with a splash of pasta water if needed for desired consistency.

steps.title: Plate
steps.content: Plate pasta, top with steak bites, drizzle any resting juices over the top, finish with parsley. Serve immediately.

notes.title: Garlic powder > fresh
notes.body: Blends smoother into a no-cook (blender-only) alfredo and avoids the raw bite that fresh garlic gives.

notes.title: Cream cheese swap
notes.body: Laughing Cow Light wedges work as the cream cheese swap; ~6 wedges ≈ 150g. Slightly tangier but the difference disappears once seasoned.

notes.title: Blender warming
notes.body: High-speed blender (Vitamix-class) for several minutes brings the sauce to serving temp without splitting. Lower-power blenders may need a quick warm in a saucepan after.

notes.title: Steak temp
notes.body: 60–90 sec/side for medium-rare on ¾" cubes. Add ~30 sec/side per doneness step.

notes.title: Macro angle
notes.body: Cottage cheese + light cream cheese yields a sauce that's dramatically higher protein and lower fat than a butter/cream/parm classic.

recipes.title: Sweet Potato Soup
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Cubed sweet potato simmered in coconut milk and chicken stock, blended smooth in the pot. Sour cream and green onion to finish. Optional sautéed chorizo for body.

steps.title: Cube
steps.content: Cube the sweet potato into ¾" pieces.

steps.title: Sweat in butter
steps.content: Heat butter in a large pot over medium. Add cubed sweet potato and cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until edges start to soften.

steps.title: Add leeks
steps.content: Stir in the chopped leeks. Cook 2 more minutes.

steps.title: Add liquids
steps.content: Pour in coconut milk and chicken stock — enough to fill the pot.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Add pepper and cayenne. If using chorizo, fold in the sautéed slices now so its fat infuses the broth.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.content: Cover and simmer about 30 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are completely fork-tender.

steps.title: Blend in pot
steps.content: Use an immersion blender to blend the soup smooth right in the pot.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Ladle into bowls. Top with a dollop of sour cream and sliced green onion.

notes.title: Coconut milk
notes.body: Full-fat is best for body. 1.5 cans = balanced; 2 cans = creamier and milder.

notes.title: Chorizo option
notes.body: Spanish-style cured chorizo (sliced and sautéed first) adds smoke and salt without overwhelming the sweet potato. The rendered fat is part of the point — fold it in with the slices.

notes.title: Stock level
notes.body: "Fill the pan" is the right instinct — about 1 quart for a standard 4-qt soup pot. Less stock = thicker, more puree-like; more = thinner, more brothy.

notes.title: Cube size
notes.body: ¾-inch cubes cook through in ~30 min. Smaller is fine but they'll start to fall apart before you blend — which is fine since you're blending anyway.

recipes.title: 7 Layer Dip
recipes.author: Kathe
recipes.description: Kathe's no-cook crowd-pleaser. Refried beans, guac, sour cream, salsa, and a fresh top of cheese, lettuce, tomato, olive. Layered, chilled, scoop with chips.

steps.title: Beans first
steps.content: Spread the refried beans evenly across the bottom of a 9×13 dish or wide shallow trifle bowl.

steps.title: Guac
steps.content: Layer the guacamole over the beans, edge to edge.

steps.title: Sour cream
steps.content: Spread the sour cream in an even layer.

steps.title: Salsa
steps.content: Spoon salsa over the sour cream — drain off any extra liquid first so the layers stay distinct.

steps.title: Cheese
steps.content: Sprinkle shredded cheese evenly across the top of the salsa.

steps.title: Lettuce
steps.content: Scatter the shredded lettuce.

steps.title: Tomatoes
steps.content: Add the diced tomatoes.

steps.title: Olives
steps.content: Finish with sliced olives.

steps.title: Chill
steps.content: Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving — gives the layers time to set so they don't slide when you scoop.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Pull from the fridge and serve with tortilla chips.

notes.title: Source
notes.body: Kathe's handwritten recipe book, attributed to "mom" on the card.

notes.title: Quantities are estimates
notes.body: The card lists ingredients only — no measurements. These work for a 9×13 dish; scale up for a deeper trifle bowl. Confirm with Kathe if you want her exact ratios.

notes.title: Layer logic
notes.body: Bottom (heaviest, most spreadable) to top (driest, garnish-like). Beans hold structure, guac/sour cream form the creamy middle, dry toppings finish on top so they don't bleed.

notes.title: Make-ahead window
notes.body: Best 1–4 hours ahead. Beyond ~6 hours the lettuce and tomatoes start weeping and layers go muddy. For longer prep, do everything except the lettuce/tomato/olive top, add those right before serving.

notes.title: Common variations
notes.body: Mix taco seasoning into the sour cream. Or blend salsa into the guac. Once you've cooked Kathe's version, capture which variant she uses as v2.

recipes.title: Steve's Margarita
recipes.author: Steve
recipes.description: Frozen blender margarita from Steve's recipe card. Rose's lime cordial does the heavy lifting; a Vitamix-class blender does the texture work.

steps.title: Salt the rim
steps.content: Run a lime wedge around the edge of each glass, then press the rim into a small plate of coarse salt to coat. Skip if you don't want a salted rim.

steps.title: Combine
steps.content: Add the tequila, triple sec, Rose's lime juice, sugar, and ice to a high-power blender.

steps.title: Blend
steps.content: Blend on high until the ice is fully crushed and the mixture is smooth and slushy, about 30–60 seconds. Stop and scrape the sides if needed.

steps.title: Pour
steps.content: Pour into the prepared glasses.

steps.title: Garnish
steps.content: Lime wheel on the rim. Cheers.

notes.title: Powerful blender required
notes.body: Written for a Vitamix or similar. Lower-power blenders will leave ice chunks — use crushed ice instead of cubes, or run the blender longer in 30-second pulses.

notes.title: Tequila choice
notes.body: 100% agave blanco / silver works best — its brightness cuts through the cold and sweetness. Reposado works too if that's what's open.

notes.title: Rose's vs fresh lime
notes.body: Built around Rose's Lime Juice — the sweetened cordial. That's what gives it the classic 70s/80s margarita profile. Subbing fresh lime juice changes the drink entirely; you'd need to add more sugar (~2 tbsp) to compensate, and it still won't taste the same.

notes.title: Sugar dial
notes.body: 1 tbsp takes the edge off the Rose's tartness. Skip for puckery, bump to 1.5 tbsp for sweeter.

notes.title: Scaling
notes.body: Scales linearly. For a pitcher: 4× quantities, blend in two batches if your blender can't handle 5 cups of ice + 5 cups of liquid at once.

recipes.title: Open Face Steak Sandwich
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Chili-rubbed sirloin on toasted baguette, jammy caramelized onions, roasted bell pepper, broiled 1835 aged cheddar, au jus on the side. The chili rub comes from Martha Stewart's chili-rubbed skirt steak — works just as well on sirloin.

steps.title: Caramelize onions
steps.content: Slice the white onion thin. Cook over medium-low in butter or oil for 25–30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden and jammy. Reserve 3/4 for the sandwich, 1/4 for the au jus.

steps.title: Roast the pepper
steps.content: Preheat oven to 500°F. Roast the bell pepper whole on a sheet pan for 20 minutes, until the skin is blistered. Transfer to a bowl, cover, let steam 10 minutes. Peel skin, remove seeds, slice into strips.

steps.title: Make the rub
steps.content: Combine chili powder, ground coriander, light brown sugar, dried oregano, coarse salt, and black pepper.

steps.title: Rub the steak
steps.content: Pat the sirloin dry. Coat all sides with the chili rub. Let rest at room temp 15–20 minutes.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Heat a cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Sear the sirloin about 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thin against the grain.

steps.title: Toast the baguette
steps.content: Drop the oven to 425°F. Halve the baguette lengthwise. Toast cut-side up about 5 minutes until the edges crisp.

steps.title: Build the au jus
steps.content: In a small saucepan, simmer the au jus with the reserved 1/4 caramelized onions for about 5 minutes to marry the flavors.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.content: Pile sliced steak on the toasted baguette. Top with caramelized onions and roasted pepper strips. Layer 1835 cheddar slices over the top.

steps.title: Broil
steps.content: Broil 1–2 minutes until the cheese is melty and bubbling. Watch it — broilers move fast.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Slice into portions. Serve with au jus on the side for dipping.

notes.title: Sirloin vs skirt
notes.body: The chili rub originates with Martha Stewart's chili-rubbed skirt steak. Sirloin works well — just sear hot and slice thin against the grain. If skirt is what's available, lean into the original.

notes.title: 1835 Cabot
notes.body: Cabot's 1835 Classic Reserve is a 12+ month aged cheddar. The aging is the point — it holds its shape under the broiler instead of breaking and going greasy, and the sharpness cuts through the chili rub.

notes.title: Pepper roast tip
notes.body: 500°F on a whole pepper gives you smoky char without overcooking. The 10-minute steam in a covered bowl after is what makes the skin peel cleanly.

notes.title: Au jus shortcut
notes.body: A packet of Johnny's or McCormick au jus base + the reserved 1/4 caramelized onions is fine. Or homemade: reduce 1 cup beef stock with a splash of red wine and a knob of butter.

notes.title: Save the trim
notes.body: If there are pepper trimmings or steak ends, chop them up and stir into the au jus too — adds depth.

recipes.title: Mahi Tacos
recipes.author: Kristen
recipes.description: Clean weeknight TJ's stack — frozen mahi seared with Chili Lime, on soft street tacos, finished with shredded cabbage and a drizzle of cilantro dressing.

steps.title: Thaw the mahi
steps.content: If frozen, thaw in the fridge overnight or run sealed bags under cold water for ~20 minutes. Pat completely dry.

steps.title: Season
steps.content: Sprinkle the chili lime seasoning generously over both sides of the fillets.

steps.title: Sear
steps.content: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil or butter in a skillet over medium-high. Cook the mahi 3–4 minutes per side until opaque and just flaking. Don't overcook — mahi is lean and goes from perfect to dry quickly.

steps.title: Flake
steps.content: Transfer fish to a cutting board, let rest 1 minute, then break into rough 1-inch chunks with a fork.

steps.title: Warm the shells
steps.content: Char the tortillas one at a time in a dry skillet over medium-high, ~20 seconds per side. Or wrap a stack in a damp towel and microwave 30 seconds.

steps.title: Build
steps.content: Shell → fish chunks → handful of shredded cabbage → drizzle of cilantro dressing.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Plate with lime wedges and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.

notes.title: Trader Joe's stack
notes.body: Built around three TJ's products — frozen mahi, the Chili Lime Seasoning, and either the Cilantro Salad Dressing or Cilantro Crema (both work, the crema is heavier). Swap in homemade or grocery equivalents if you don't shop there.

notes.title: Doneness cue
notes.body: Mahi is done when the flesh is opaque and just starts to flake when nudged with a fork. The center should be barely translucent — it'll finish carrying over off the heat.

notes.title: Air fryer alternative
notes.body: 380°F for 7–8 minutes, no flipping needed. Slightly easier than the skillet, less browning.

notes.title: Cabbage prep
notes.body: Toss the shredded cabbage with a pinch of salt and a squeeze of lime 5 minutes before serving — softens it and brings out the flavor.

notes.title: Spice dial
notes.body: TJ's Chili Lime is mild. Bump with a pinch of cayenne in the seasoning, or a few dashes of hot sauce on the finished taco.

recipes.title: Enchilada
recipes.author: Kristen
recipes.description: Kitchen-sink enchilada — rotisserie chicken, beans, and chicken rice rolled in tortillas, baked under sauce and cheese, finished with cold sour cream / lettuce / olives.

ingredients.name: can refried or black beans (15 oz)
cooked chicken-flavored rice (Spanish rice or Knorr)

steps.title: Preheat
steps.content: Oven to 400°F.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.content: In a large bowl, combine shredded rotisserie chicken, beans, rice, 1 cup of the cheese, and ~1/2 cup of the enchilada sauce. Stir to coat everything.

steps.title: Warm the tortillas
steps.content: Wrap a stack in a damp paper towel and microwave 30 seconds, or char briefly in a dry skillet. Pliable tortillas don't crack when rolled.

steps.title: Sauce the pan
steps.content: Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce in a 9×13 baking dish.

steps.title: Roll
steps.content: Spoon ~1/2 cup filling down the center of each tortilla. Roll tightly. Place seam-down in the pan.

steps.title: Top
steps.content: Pour remaining enchilada sauce evenly over the rolled enchiladas. Sprinkle the remaining 1 cup of cheese on top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.content: 400°F for 15–20 minutes until cheese is fully melted and sauce bubbles at the edges.

steps.title: Garnish cold
steps.content: Pull from oven, let rest 2 minutes, then top with sour cream, shredded lettuce, and sliced olives. Serve immediately.

notes.title: Cold-vs-hot logic
notes.body: The card lists lettuce inside the rolled filling, but lettuce wilts in a hot oven. The standard family-enchilada move — and what's written here — is to garnish lettuce/sour cream/olives after baking.

notes.title: Beans choice
notes.body: Refried gives a creamier, more bound filling. Black beans give texture and definition. Either works. Drain and rinse the black beans if using.

notes.title: Tortilla choice
notes.body: Flour tortillas hold up to the rolling and the sauce without breaking. Corn is more traditional but tears easily — heat them well first if going corn.

notes.title: Make-ahead
notes.body: Assemble fully (steps 1–6), cover, refrigerate up to 24 hours. Bake 25–30 minutes from cold instead of 15–20.

recipes.title: Fajita
recipes.author: Kathe and Kristen
recipes.description: Cast-iron flank steak fajitas — seared steak, jammy onions, charred bell peppers, warm tortillas, sour cream. Optional citrus-cumin marinade for the steak when you have an extra hour.

ingredients.name: bell peppers (1 red, 1 green — sliced strips)

steps.title: Season the steak
steps.content: Pat the flank steak dry. Rub all over with salt, pepper, cumin, chili powder, and smoked paprika. If marinating, add lime juice + garlic and rest in the fridge 1–4 hours; otherwise let it sit at room temp 20 minutes.

steps.title: Slice the vegetables
steps.content: Cut peppers into ¼" strips. Cut onion into thick half-moons.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.content: Heat 1 tbsp olive oil in a cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking. Sear flank steak 3–4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Transfer to a cutting board.

steps.title: Rest
steps.content: Let the steak rest 5–7 minutes — non-negotiable for flank steak. Cook the vegetables while it rests.

steps.title: Caramelize onions, then peppers
steps.content: In the same pan (don't wipe — fond is flavor), add the remaining 1 tbsp oil. Add onions, cook 5–7 minutes over medium-high until edges char and they go jammy. Add peppers, cook another 4–5 minutes until softened with some bite remaining.

steps.title: Slice the steak
steps.content: Cut the rested steak THIN and AGAINST the grain. Grain runs lengthwise; cut perpendicular to it.

steps.title: Warm the tortillas
steps.content: Char each tortilla over an open flame or in a dry skillet ~15 seconds per side until pliable and lightly toasted. Stack in a clean towel to keep warm.

steps.title: Build
steps.content: Tortilla → steak slices → onion-pepper mix → dollop of sour cream → squeeze of lime → fresh cilantro.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Set everything out family-style — let people build their own. Salsa, hot sauce, guac on the side.

notes.title: Slice against the grain
notes.body: Critical for flank steak. The grain on flank is obvious — long parallel lines running the length of the cut. Cut perpendicular to those lines, thin (¼" or less). Wrong-direction slicing makes it chewy.

notes.title: Marinade decision
notes.body: Skip the marinade for a fast weeknight version (just dry-rub seasoning is plenty). Use it if you have time and want extra tang and depth — 1 hour is good, 4 hours is better, >8 starts to mush the texture.

notes.title: Steak temp
notes.body: 3–4 min/side gets medium-rare on 1"-thick flank. Add ~1 min/side for medium. Pull at 130°F internal; carryover brings it to 135°F during the rest.

notes.title: Cast iron is the move
notes.body: The high heat and fond development matter. Nonstick won't get the same char on the steak or vegetables.

notes.title: Variations
notes.body: Add chicken (boneless thighs cut into strips, cooked similarly) for chicken fajitas. Throw a handful of Trader Joe's Chili Lime in with the seasoning for a different lift.

recipes.title: Asado Negro
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: The Caracas Sunday dinner. Dark-caramel braise with papelón, sofrito, and a slow oven cook that turns a whole muscle into something you slice across the grain and serve with rice and fried plantain. The sauce is nearly black, glossy, and the deepest beef thing on the table.

ingredients.name: beef eye of round (tied) or chuck shoulder, one piece
ají dulce (4-6), or sweet banana pepper sub
papelón (or dark brown sugar + 1 tsp molasses)
ripe plantains (yellow with black spots), for tajadas

steps.title: Marinate (12–24 hours ahead)
steps.content: Pat beef dry. Rub all over with salt, pepper, and cumin. Blend onions, bell pepper, ají dulce, garlic, cilantro stems, Worcestershire, and olive oil to a coarse purée. Coat the beef in a sealed container. Refrigerate 12–24 hours, turning once.

steps.title: Bring to temp
steps.content: Pull beef from the fridge 45 minutes before cooking. Scrape marinade off and reserve it. Pat the beef as dry as you can — wet meat won't sear into the caramel.

steps.title: Build the caramel
steps.content: Heat neutral oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium. Add chopped papelón. Let it melt and darken to nearly black, swirling — don't stir. This is the moment to trust: it should look ruined.

steps.title: Sear into the caramel
steps.content: Lower the beef carefully into the dark caramel. Sear hard on every side, turning every 2–3 minutes, until coated in a mahogany-black crust.

steps.title: Cook the sofrito
steps.content: Remove beef to a plate. Add reserved marinade to the pot — it will sizzle aggressively. Cook, stirring, until onions soften and the raw garlic smell mellows.

steps.title: Build the braise
steps.content: Stir in tomato paste, cook 1 minute. Pour in red wine, scrape the bottom clean. Reduce 3 minutes. Return the beef. Add stock to come about 2/3 of the way up the meat. Add bay leaves and dark soy. Bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Oven braise
steps.content: Cover. Transfer to a 150°C / 300°F oven. Turn the beef every 45 minutes. It's done when a fork slides in with no resistance — eye of round in about 3 hours, chuck closer to 3.5.

steps.title: Rest and reduce
steps.content: Remove beef to a board, tent loosely with foil. Rest 20 minutes. Meanwhile, on the stovetop, reduce the braising liquid over medium-high until it coats a spoon — 8–12 minutes. Strain through a fine mesh if you want it sleek; leave it as-is for a rustic version.

steps.title: Tajadas
steps.content: Slice plantains lengthwise into 1 cm strips. Fry in neutral oil at 175°C / 350°F until deeply caramelized, 2–3 minutes per side. Drain on a rack and salt lightly.

steps.title: Serve
steps.content: Slice beef across the grain into 1 cm rounds. Plate over white rice, ladle sauce generously, tajadas on the side. Sauce intensifies on day 2 and 3 — make extra.

notes.title: Choosing the beef
notes.body: Traditional cut is muchacho redondo — eye of round, lean and uniform, tied to hold its cylindrical shape. It slices cleanly into rounds. Chuck shoulder works beautifully too and is more forgiving (more fat = harder to overcook); the slices won't be as photogenic but the eating is better.

notes.title: No red wine option
notes.body: Replace the 240 ml red wine with 180 ml additional beef stock + 30 ml balsamic vinegar + 30 ml pomegranate juice (or unsweetened cranberry). You lose some structural acidity from wine tannins but gain back depth from balsamic and the dark fruit.

notes.title: Papelón sub
notes.body: 80 g dark brown sugar + 1 tsp molasses. Real papelón (also called panela) has a slight bitter funk that brown sugar can't quite replicate but it's close enough.

notes.title: Ají dulce
notes.body: The soul of Venezuelan cooking — looks like a habanero but is sweet, not hot. Sub: sweet banana pepper, or in a pinch half a yellow bell + a pinch of allspice.

notes.title: Make ahead
notes.body: The whole dish improves overnight. Slice cold beef, return to warm sauce, gently rewarm covered. Serve.

notes.title: Cross-format note
notes.body: Structurally the same move as the Sichuan red-braise: take sugar past where it looks ruined, sear protein into the bitter caramel, slow braise with aromatics. Vietnamese thịt kho and Cantonese red-braised pork live in the same family.

recipes.title: Sichuan Caramel-Braised Beef Shoulder
recipes.author: Kenneth
recipes.description: Red-braise (红烧) built on the classic tang se (糖色) technique: sugar cooked past golden into deep mahogany, just shy of bitter. With Pixian doubanjiang, whole Sichuan peppercorns, and a baking soda velvet — glassy sauce, melting cubes, slow-building heat.

ingredients.name: beef shoulder or chuck, cut into 4–5 cm cubes

steps.title: Velvet the beef
steps.content: Toss beef with baking soda and salt. Let rest at room temp 30–60 minutes. Rinse thoroughly under cold water, then pat very dry with paper towels. Dryness matters for the next step.

steps.title: Build the caramel
steps.content: Heat oil in a heavy Dutch oven over medium. Add sugar. As it melts, swirl the pan occasionally — do not stir. Cook past golden, past amber, into deep mahogany. A faint wisp of smoke is fine. The bitterness becomes depth once the beef hits it.

steps.title: Sear in the caramel
steps.content: Add beef carefully — it will splatter and the caramel will seize. Toss to coat every cube in the dark glaze. The caramel re-melts as the beef releases moisture.

steps.title: Bloom the doubanjiang
steps.content: Push beef to one side. Add doubanjiang to the rendered oil. Fry 30–60 seconds until the oil glows red and the paste smells nutty rather than raw.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.content: Add chilies, Sichuan peppercorns, ginger, garlic, onion, star anise, and cassia. Stir to combine.

steps.title: Deglaze and braise
steps.content: Pour in Shaoxing wine, scrape the bottom. Add both soy sauces and water/stock to just cover. Bring to a boil, reduce to a low simmer, cover, and braise 1.5 hours.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.content: Add potatoes and carrots. Continue simmering, partially covered, until vegetables are tender and the sauce has reduced to a glossy nappé that coats a spoon.

steps.title: Finish
steps.content: Taste — adjust with a pinch of salt or a few drops of soy if needed. Top with scallions. Rest 10 minutes off heat before serving; the sauce thickens as it cools.

notes.title: Why the baking soda matters
notes.body: Tossing diced beef with baking soda and salt for 30–60 minutes (then rinsing) raises the surface pH and disrupts protein bonds. The result: cubes that stay tender through a long braise and absorb sauce without going stringy. Don't skip this step.

notes.title: Better on day 2 and 3
notes.body: Fat re-emulsifies, heat mellows into warmth, potatoes drink everything. Stays great 5+ days in the fridge.

notes.title: Heat level
notes.body: 8 dried chilies whole give moderate heat. Break them for more, or toast them in the oil before the caramel step for smokier depth.

notes.title: Without doubanjiang
notes.body: Not the same dish, but you can sub 2 tbsp red miso + 1 tbsp gochujang in a pinch.

notes.title: Sub for rock sugar
notes.body: Granulated works; the sauce is slightly less glossy.

notes.title: Serve with
notes.body: Jasmine rice, smashed cucumber salad with garlic + black vinegar + chili oil, blanched gai lan.

notes.title: Cross-format note
notes.body: The dark-caramel-braise technique here is the same structural move as Vietnamese thịt kho, Cantonese red-braised pork, and Venezuelan Asado Negro. The bitter-caramel sear creates a flavor floor that no late-stage seasoning can substitute for. Worth treating as a technique class, not a recipe.

recipes.title: Key Lime Pie
recipes.author: Kenneth and Claude
recipes.description: The most balanced of three GF crust directions. Toasted pecans, almond flour, and oats bound with butter and a tablespoon of honey — the honey is what makes it sing. Goes elevated dinner pie.

ingredients.name: key lime juice (fresh or Nellie & Joe's bottled)
lime curl or fresh zest (for garnish)

steps.title: Toast pecans
steps.content: Preheat oven to 350°F. Spread pecan halves on a sheet pan, toast 5–7 minutes until fragrant. Cool completely.

steps.title: Build the crust
steps.content: In a food processor, pulse pecans + oats together until pecans are a coarse meal and oats are partly broken. Pulse in almond flour, brown sugar, salt, cinnamon. Add melted butter and honey, pulse until the mixture clumps.

steps.title: Press
steps.content: Press firmly and evenly into a 9" pie plate, building up the sides. Use the flat bottom of a measuring cup for an even crust.

steps.title: Pre-bake the crust
steps.content: Bake 10–12 minutes until edges are golden. Cool slightly while you make the filling — warm crust + filling = better seal.

steps.title: Whisk yolks
steps.content: In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with lime zest for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thickened.

steps.title: Add condensed milk
steps.content: Whisk in the sweetened condensed milk until smooth.

steps.title: Add lime juice
steps.content: Stream the lime juice in slowly while whisking. The mixture will thicken visibly — that's the acid starting to set the proteins.

steps.title: Bake the pie
steps.content: Pour filling into warm crust. Bake 12–15 minutes until the center has just the faintest wobble when you nudge it.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.content: Cool on a rack to room temp. Cover and chill at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

steps.title: Whip and serve
steps.content: Whip cold heavy cream with powdered sugar and vanilla to medium peaks. Top the pie (or dollop per slice). Garnish with a lime curl or fresh zest.

notes.title: Why honey
notes.body: The honey isn't just sweetness — it brings the malted-floral note that mimics graham flour. Don't skip it.

notes.title: Toasting matters
notes.body: Raw pecans give you a flat crust. Toasted pecans give you depth. 5–7 minutes makes the difference between fine and great.

notes.title: Pre-bake the crust
notes.body: Filling on raw crust gets soggy. The crust needs heat first.

notes.title: The wobble test
notes.body: Pie is done when the center moves like jello when you nudge the pan. If it moves like liquid, bake another 2–3 minutes. If it's set solid, you've overshot — still delicious, just denser.

notes.title: Bottled key lime juice
notes.body: Nellie & Joe's is what most Florida bakeries use. Fresh key lime is more aromatic but the juice ratio is fragile — bottled is more consistent.

notes.title: Make ahead
notes.body: Whole pie keeps 3 days covered in the fridge. Top with whipped cream right before serving.

recipes.title: Key Lime Pie
recipes.author: Kenneth and Claude
recipes.description: The most fun of three crust variants. GF gingersnaps + butter + salt + a doubled-down hit of ground ginger. Molasses warmth meets lime acid the way a moscow mule does — assertive, balanced, addictive. The easiest of the three.

ingredients.name: GF gingersnaps (Tate's or similar; about 2 cups crumbs)
key lime juice (fresh or Nellie & Joe's bottled)
lime curl or fresh zest (for garnish)

steps.title: Preheat
steps.content: Oven to 350°F.

steps.title: Crumb the cookies
steps.content: Pulse gingersnaps in a food processor to fine crumbs — about 2 cups. (Or seal in a bag and crush with a rolling pin.)

steps.title: Build the crust
steps.content: Combine crumbs, melted butter, ground ginger, and salt. Mix until the crumbs are evenly damp like wet sand.

steps.title: Press
steps.content: Press firmly into a 9" pie plate, building up the sides. Use the flat bottom of a measuring cup for an even crust.

steps.title: Pre-bake
steps.content: Bake 8 minutes until set and aromatic. Cool slightly while you make the filling — warm crust + filling = better seal.

steps.title: Whisk yolks
steps.content: In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with lime zest for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thickened.

steps.title: Add condensed milk
steps.content: Whisk in the sweetened condensed milk until smooth.

steps.title: Add lime juice
steps.content: Stream the lime juice in slowly while whisking. The mixture will thicken visibly — that's the acid starting to set the proteins.

steps.title: Bake the pie
steps.content: Pour filling into warm crust. Bake 12–15 minutes until the center has just the faintest wobble when you nudge it.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.content: Cool on a rack to room temp. Cover and chill at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

steps.title: Whip and serve
steps.content: Whip cold heavy cream with powdered sugar and vanilla to medium peaks. Top the pie (or dollop per slice). Garnish with a lime curl or fresh zest.

notes.title: The doubled ginger
notes.body: 0.5 tsp added ground ginger amplifies what's already in the gingersnap. Halve if you want it subtler; bump to 1 tsp for punchier.

notes.title: Crumb fineness
notes.body: Pulse to a fine even crumb. Larger chunks don't bind as tightly and leave gaps.

notes.title: Cookie brands
notes.body: Tate's GF Gingersnaps are easy to find and clean-tasting. Pamela's also works. Don't add brown sugar — gingersnaps are sweet enough on their own.

notes.title: Why pre-bake
notes.body: 8 minutes sets the crumbs into a cohesive shell. Skipping this gives you a sandy, falling-apart crust.

notes.title: Pairing
notes.body: A moscow mule on the side is no joke. The lime-ginger axis carries cleanly between pie and cocktail.

recipes.title: Key Lime Pie
recipes.author: Kenneth and Claude
recipes.description: The deeply Floridian one. Toasted shredded coconut + ground macadamia, bound with butter and an egg white that keeps the coconut from shrinking. Tastes like Key West smells. The "did you make this?" answer.

ingredients.name: key lime juice (fresh or Nellie & Joe's bottled)
lime curl or toasted coconut (for garnish)

steps.title: Preheat
steps.content: Oven to 350°F.

steps.title: Grind the macadamia
steps.content: Pulse macadamia nuts in a food processor to a coarse meal — stop before they release oil and turn pasty. About 6–8 quick pulses.

steps.title: Build the crust
steps.content: Add shredded coconut, coconut flour, brown sugar, and salt to the food processor. Pulse a few times to combine. Add melted butter and egg white, pulse until the mixture holds together when pressed.

steps.title: Press
steps.content: Press firmly into a 9" pie plate, building up the sides. Use the flat bottom of a measuring cup.

steps.title: Pre-bake
steps.content: Bake 10 minutes, watching closely — coconut browns FAST. Pull when edges are just turning golden. If it's getting dark at 8 minutes, take it out.

steps.title: Whisk yolks
steps.content: In a bowl, whisk egg yolks with lime zest for 1–2 minutes until pale and slightly thickened.

steps.title: Add condensed milk
steps.content: Whisk in the sweetened condensed milk until smooth.

steps.title: Add lime juice
steps.content: Stream the lime juice in slowly while whisking. The mixture will thicken visibly — that's the acid starting to set the proteins.

steps.title: Bake the pie
steps.content: Pour filling into warm crust. Bake 12–15 minutes until the center has just the faintest wobble when you nudge it.

steps.title: Cool and chill
steps.content: Cool on a rack to room temp. Cover and chill at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.

steps.title: Whip and serve
steps.content: Whip cold heavy cream with powdered sugar and vanilla to medium peaks. Top the pie. Garnish with a lime curl and a sprinkle of toasted coconut.

notes.title: Watch the crust
notes.body: Coconut burns faster than anything else in this recipe. Set a timer for 8 minutes minimum, then check every 30 seconds. Pull at first sign of deep golden.

notes.title: Why the egg white
notes.body: Coconut shrinks and clumps when baked because it loses moisture. The egg white provides protein structure that holds the crust together. Don't skip it.

notes.title: Don't over-pulse macadamia
notes.body: They have so much oil that another 30 seconds takes them from meal to butter. Aim for coarse and stop.

notes.title: Macadamia source
notes.body: Whole raw macadamia from a bulk bin is cheaper than packaged. They oxidize quickly — store in the freezer.

notes.title: Pair with
notes.body: Aged rum on ice. Doesn't need anything else.

recipes.title: Sweet Pickled Celery
recipes.author: Kenneth (inspired by Nomad East, SLC)
recipes.description: Inspired by Nomad East in Salt Lake City — bright, sweet, lemon-zest forward. Cured 2 weeks for full flavor.

ingredients.name: lemon zest strip per jar (about 2", no pith)
large bunch celery (sliced on a bias ¼" thick, 6–7 cups)

steps.title: Make brine
steps.content: Combine vinegar, water, sugar, salt, peppercorns, and celery seed in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, stirring until sugar and salt dissolve.

steps.title: Zest the jars
steps.content: Place one strip of lemon zest in each sterilized pint jar.

steps.title: Pack
steps.content: Pack raw celery tightly into jars, leaving ½" headspace.

steps.title: Brine and de-bubble
steps.content: Ladle hot brine over celery, maintaining ½" headspace. Remove air bubbles with a chopstick or bubble tool.

steps.title: Seal
steps.content: Wipe rims clean, apply lids and bands finger-tight.

steps.title: Process
steps.content: Process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes. (Adjust for altitude: add 5 minutes above 6,000 feet.)

steps.title: Cure
steps.content: Let jars rest 24 hours. Check seals. Cure at least 2 weeks before opening for best flavor.

notes.title: More sweetness
notes.body: Increase sugar to 1¼ cups.

notes.title: Brighter citrus
notes.body: Add a second zest strip or try Meyer lemon.

notes.title: Warmer profile
notes.body: Add a coin of fresh ginger or a cracked cardamom pod.

notes.title: Deeper complexity
notes.body: Substitute ½ cup apple cider vinegar for part of the rice vinegar.
